metadata.title: Rabi Oscillation — Spin Flopping Between Up and Down
metadata.purpose: Critique of the qm2-rabi-oscillation D3 sim: dual-chart encoding, two fixable bugs
metadata.reformat: center-cut, focus-aware; pantry/<bid>-916.* is the human replacement slot; -916 overrides honored

beats.narration_text: Salut. Liam — in for Bear. Someone handed Claude one prompt: write me a visualization for Rabi oscillation, spin flipping between up and down. Here's what came back. We're judging the viz, not the physics.

props.command: Hey Claude, write me a visualization for Rabi oscillation — spin flipping between up and down.
props.segment: Rabi Oscillation — Spin Flopping Between Up and Down

beats.narration_text: White page, two charts. Left: Spin Probability vs Time — P↑ in blue and P↓ in gray, both oscillating between zero and one over four microseconds. A red dashed time marker advances in real time, colored dots riding each curve. Right: a circle labeled Bloch sphere, a red state-vector arrow sweeping its boundary, leaving a faint trace. Above: two sliders — Rabi frequency and initial polar angle — a play button, and a live readout of P↑, P↓, their sum, and the period.

Drag the Rabi frequency slider from one megahertz up to five. The oscillation accelerates: period drops from 1.0 to 0.2 microseconds in the readout, the background curves compress, the Bloch arrow spins faster. The equation being animated is P↑(t) equals cosine-squared of omega-zero t over two. The prediction the sim asks you to test: at twice the frequency, does the spin flip twice as fast? Yes. Every element confirms it.

Three things land. One: the subtitle front-loads the physics contract before the animation runs — deterministic spin flip, no measurement, no collapse. That single line rules out the most common misread of Rabi as a collapse event. Two: the P↑ plus P↓ readout holds at 1.0000 regardless of what you drag. Unitarity isn't implied — it's verified live. Three: both charts run simultaneously — probability over time and the Bloch sphere. Same oscillation, two representations, synchronized time marker. Students can build one picture and check it against the other.

Let's recap with Claude. Useful for day-one NMR. Deterministic spin flip shown in two representations. Unitarity held as a live invariant. But the x-axis lies when omega changes, and the Bloch sphere labels the wrong plane. Fix those two — one class attribute, one label string — and this becomes a clean demonstration.

artifactLines: Deterministic spin flip in two representations
Bloch sphere: wrong plane, wrong eigenstate label

beats.narration_text: Your turn. Paste this into Claude: I have a Rabi oscillation D3 simulation with two bugs. First, the x-axis tick labels freeze when the Rabi frequency slider moves — the axis group was never given the CSS class the remove selector expects. Fix: add .attr class x-axis on creation and rebind the axis on each input event. Second, the Bloch sphere is labeled x–z plane but the trajectory lives in y–z under H equals omega-zero S-x. Fix: change the plane label to y–z and the equator marker from |+⟩ to |+y⟩. Return only the corrected lines of code with enough context to place them.
